items.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016
items.q: I managed to get a gig with the both of them and Dolores Mancuso at the Beeches.

ctx.x: Oh man, I can’t tell you how much Dick Robilatto, what kind of influence he had on my life. And I was lucky enough that I got him on the phone not too long before he passed away. I’m not even sure he knew for certain who he was talking to. But he said, “Yeah I had a student Charlie who went out to L.A. I think he’s doing okay out there.” And it was just so touching. He was my high school band director. He was such a wonderful guy. But that’s, you know I have said time and time again I feel such a debt to the…

I’ve told Rick and Carmen that too. Because when I first moved up here I managed to get a gig with the both of them and Dolores Mancuso at the Beeches. And I just sat on my stool with my sax and I watched and listened to what they did. And I thought I knew a lot because I had gone to music school. But I didn’t know anything about playing gigs and filling what people’s expectations would be, or beyond. It was really an education for me.

Yeah. Playing here in the years that I did before I went to L.A. was just priceless. And I told Carmen yesterday, because Carmen pulled me in on a project in L.A. before I moved there. It was centered around a percussionist who played in the group Traffic. And his name was Rebop Kwaku Baah. He was a Nigerian prince percussionist. And Carmen had gotten a call from a piano player who was a guy that was Lou Rawls’ music director, Reg Powell, and a drummer, Jack Toker, lives in Seattle. And Reg was kind of putting…
